c.tagline: Tanzania's steamy Indian Ocean metropolis - harbour bustle, Swahili markets, and the gateway to Zanzibar.

taxi.color: no official uniform color; often white or branded
taxi.fareNote: Meters are rare, so agree the fare before you set off, or use app-based Uber or Bolt for transparent, prepaid pricing.

emergency.note: 112 is the general emergency number reachable from any mobile network; 114 reaches police. Private ambulance and medevac services also operate for tourists.

hood_landmark.City Centre / Kivukoni: St Joseph Cathedral Dar es Salaam
hood_landmark.Oyster Bay: Coco Beach Oyster Bay Dar es Salaam

avoid.reason: Petty crime and bag-snatching in the centre; caution at night and on isolated beaches

hood_desc: Dar's downtown core along the harbour front, home to the Askari Monument, St Joseph's Cathedral, the National Museum, and the Zanzibar ferry terminal; central and busy, best for sightseeing and transport links.

An upmarket, leafy peninsula district full of embassies, expat apartments, and the city's best restaurants, cafes, and bars, plus the Slipway waterfront complex; the top pick for dining and nightlife.

A relaxed, upscale seaside neighbourhood along Coco Beach and Toure Drive, with boutique hotels, ocean-view dining, and weekend beach crowds; suits travellers wanting calm and sea breezes near the action.
Dar's frenetic central market district, a maze of stalls and wholesale shops selling everything from spices to textiles; loud, authentic, and best for budget travellers and immersive local shopping.
A laid-back beach suburb reached by the historic ferry or the Kigamboni Bridge, fringed with palm-shaded sands and low-key beach resorts; a quiet escape from the city bustle.
lodging: Hyatt Regency Dar es Salaam, The Kilimanjaro
Protea Hotel by Marriott Dar es Salaam Oyster Bay

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: DART buses and daladalas generally run about 5am-11pm with limited late-night service; ride-hailing apps operate 24/7 and are the recommended option after dark.
transit.note: Traffic congestion is severe at peak hours. The DART bus rapid transit (Mwendokasi) runs on dedicated lanes, cheap daladala minibuses cover everywhere else, and ferries cross to Kigamboni and to Zanzibar; many visitors rely on Uber or Bolt for comfort.
transit.pay: DART fares use a smart card or cash at station gates; daladalas are paid in cash to the conductor. Ferry and Zanzibar tickets are bought at the terminal counters.

ferry: Zanzibar fast ferries (Azam Marine / Zan Fast)
train: Tanzania SGR (Standard Gauge Railway to Morogoro / Dodoma)

transit.m: Daladala minibus toward the city centre (~45-75 min)
Taxi or ride-hail to the city centre (30-45 min)

tip.r: Around 10% at tourist restaurants if no service charge is added; small tips for guides, drivers, and hotel staff are appreciated.
